Issued at 249 PM EST Wed Nov 18 2026

This afternoon's upper level pattern as depicted by GOES water vapor 
imagery and RAP analysis features sprawling high pressure dominating 
much of the eastern half of the CONUS with a negatively tilted 
trough beginning to lift out of the northern Rockies. An attendant 
1000 mb surface low is located over western North Dakota. Closer to 
home, Upper Michigan is situated in a warm southwest flow regime 
between the two upper level features, promoting high in the 50s 
across the UP today with a few locations even getting into the 60s 
in the west as of early afternoon. A tightening pressure gradient 
between high pressure to the east and low pressure to the west is 
yielding breezy conditions with southwest winds gusting to 15-25 mph 
across much of the area. These warm and breezy conditions are also 
leading to some limited fire weather concerns this afternoon with 
relative humidity values starting to dip into the 30s over the 
western half of the UP.

Continued southwest flow ahead of the trough as it lifts into the 
northern Plains tonight will yield another night of mild low 
temperatures mostly in the 40s. The upper trough and its surface 
reflection will move into northern Ontario by Thursday morning. This 
will keep any precipitation well north of the area on Thursday, but 
windy conditions will persists and even ramp up further as a potent 
low level jet of 50-60 kt at 850 mb moves across the area this 
evening through Thursday. Model soundings suggest improved mixing 
depths on Thursday which will help at least some of this mix down to 
the surface, resulting in widespread gusts of 25 to 35 mph on 
Thursday. Current probabilities for advisory level gusts of 45+ mph 
are around 30-50% in the Keweenaw and closer to 10-40% for other 
favored downslope area near Lake Superior, decreasing with eastward 
extent. Have opted against any headlines for now, but this may 
warrant further consideration over the next 12-24 hours if 
conditions continue to look favorable for some higher end gusts. In 
addition to the windy conditions, expect another warm day with highs 
in the 50s. This will result in another day of limited fire weather 
concerns as minimum RH values once again threaten to dip into the 
30s.

Winds diminish Thursday night into Friday as high pressure moves 
back overhead in the wake of the system. This will allows to dip 
closer to freezing away from the lakeshores on Thursday night. Highs 
will again be in the 50s on Friday, potentially threatening daily 
record values in a few locations. This weekend will bring a pattern 
change as a shortwave ejecting out of the Desert Southwest phases 
with a deep trough moving out of western Canada in the vicinity of 
the Upper Great Lakes. This will bring rain back to the region 
beginning later Saturday as a cold front crosses the UP. 
Precipitation amounts do not look overly impressive, but the NBM 
does give a 20-40% chance for an inch or more of rain across the 
area through Sunday evening. Would expect precipitation type to be 
mostly rain through the day on Sunday as one more day of highs in the 
50s gives way to highs int he 40s on Sunday. A northerly lake effect 
snow regime looks to kick in on the back side of the system Sunday 
night into Monday, but this will be relatively short lived as most 
guidance favors high pressure building back into the region by 
Tuesday. Current NBM guidance shows around a 20-40% chance for 2 
inches of snow through Monday evening over the western half of the 
UP, with the highest probabilities over the Keweenaw and the higher 
terrain of the Porkies and the Michigamme Highlands. Much like last 
week, would expect more minimal potential accumulations closer to 
the lakeshore where temperatures will be warmer.
